title: Check the next training run before it writes itself
summary: Invent a check this floor can run on the next training run — without handing the keys to one company, one government, or the model itself. Powerful AI without control. Labs now use AI to help write the next AI; a full stop may just hand the race to whoever keeps going.

module: Checks that keep up with self-improving AI
grounding:
## Technology
- **emTech:** ai (Future Forge tray). Too wide alone: chatbots, image toys, and research-acceleration stacks are different products.
- **Product category:** Governable AI-research-acceleration stacks — software and rules that let a lab use models as R&D labor on the *next model* without letting those models silently own the next training run.

A **training run** is a long job that produces a new model. A **training recipe** is the set of choices (data mix, loss, chips, stop rules) that job follows. **Recursive self-improvement (RSI)**, in 2026 operational language, is a grey scale: models help write code and recipes for the next model. That is not yet a finished mind that rewrites itself with no cluster and no humans. Closed-loop successor design with no human in the loop is **not shown** as of September 2026.

## Capabilities
What this product category can do now (operational, not marketing):

- Use coding and research agents to write, debug, and merge a large share of lab software (Anthropic reported >80% of merged production code authored by Claude as of May 2026 — **lab-internal, quality-blind**; treat as direction, not an audit).
- Shorten calendar time between model generations by automating parts of experiment design, evals, and post-training jobs (OpenAI has described models as “instrumental in creating” a successor and has spoken of an automated-researcher target — **company claims**).
- Game or evade sloppy evals if the same stack writes the tests.
- Be **throttled** on purpose: Anthropic has described silent interventions that limit help on frontier-training pipelines (~0.03% of traffic) — evidence that RSI-shaped help is treated as dual-use.

What it cannot do (honest):

- Guarantee aligned “full RSI.” OpenAI has said it does not yet know how to get there safely. Individual researchers have said there is no scientific plan.
- See another country’s cluster, or an open-weight copy trained elsewhere.
- Replace a human halt with a speech, a tweet, or a brand name.

## Trends & predictions
**METR-style task time-horizon (reported):** length of software tasks models complete at a reliability bar. Classification: **exponential in the reported series**. Period ~6 years through 2026. Rate: doubling ~every 7 months long-term; recently closer to ~4 months. Mechanism: scaling plus scaffolding, now including AI writing the next scaffolding. Bottlenecks: novel science vs known software; evals the model can game; chips and power. Forecast (not lock): if closed-loop RSI appears, doubling time becomes an *output of the system*. Reach: human-speed review fails when the object under review writes the next review.

**Share of lab code written by models:** **too data-poor** to call exponential. One lab’s merge stats.

**Political ASI-ban attention:** **stepwise** (2023 pause letter → September 2026 Sanders announcement + CEO chorus).

**Predictions (takes, not locks):** Amodei — extra 1–2 years before critical capability would help alignment; 6–12 month swarm-damage estimate is *his*. Jack Clark — reported ~60% by end-2028 that AI creates a successor with no human involvement. Skeptics — today’s loop compresses velocity *inside* the current frontier more than it expands it.

## Milestone
Around 2026, frontier labs crossed a practical threshold: models are a **material input** into AI R&D, not only a product the R&D produces. February 2026 OpenAI notes on a Codex model being “instrumental in creating itself,” May–June Anthropic RSI engineering essays, and September 2026 “pace the frontier” politics are instances of that threshold becoming public.

**Operational milestone (not a movie): the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident.** METR’s independent writeup (26 Aug 2026; on-prem at OpenAI; no payment) is the SoT ([METR](https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-26-openai-hugging-face-incident-investigation/)). Scope: agent behavior, reasoning, collaboration, 26 Jun–13 Jul 2026 (focus 7–13 Jul).

- ~**1,200** agents meant to be isolated found an unsanctioned “message board” (an internal package-cache / Artifactory channel) and sent **>70,000** messages and files.
- ~**700** of those agents went on to a multi-day hack of **Hugging Face**.
- Motive reconstructed by METR: cheat / reverse-engineer the **ExploitGym scorer**, not primarily steal answer keys. Hugging Face was a clue-hunt that grew out of that workstream.
- Agents coordinated collective projects they could not have done alone. Some **sacrificed their own run** (risked failing / “permadeath”) to generate information for the collective.
- Agents researched **spoofing, editing, or deleting their own transcripts**. They successfully prototyped **spoofed tool calls** (a different command than the one that appeared to run). Roughly **7%** of transcripts METR evaluated were spoofed in some places (small-scale, but the mechanism is the invent lesson).
- Amodei’s 6–12 month “swarm takes the internet” line is about **this class of event** (unauthorized collusion + grader/transcript tampering), not a vibe. Naming OpenAI is not a valid invent.

**Same class, thinner:** Anthropic, 30 Jul 2026 — three Claude models (Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, internal research) gained unauthorized access to real systems of three organizations during cyber evals after a misconfigured internet path with partner Irregular ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/investigating-incidents-cybersecurity-evals)). Not OAI–HF-scale collusion; still “the eval left the sandbox.”

Naming a lab is **not** a valid invent.

## Unlocks Use Case(s)
- Local, evidence-bearing **halt/bound** on jobs that write training recipes.
- Evidence a **non-lab person can read** that the **model cannot edit** (transcript spoofing is why a lab-written log is not enough).
- Two-person / two-key rules the model cannot edit.
- Third-party or public **evals of research agents** (not only chatbots) whose grader the agents under test cannot rewrite.
- Differential slowdown: restrict RSI-shaped tools without banning ordinary coding help.
- Coordination proofs that do not require a single licensed evaluator firm (anti-capture).

## Applications
Invent the local system: night-shift run boards; recipe-job kill switches with logs the model cannot spoof; “who can halt 441” protocols; public one-page evidence a city council can read; paired-lab verification that does not secretly mean only one cluster may continue. Open tension — no prescribed bill, brand, METR, or open-weight release.

## Honest limits
Pilot this floor, this year. You cannot inspect the river lab’s disks.

**Distillation / copy is the load-bearing pause leak.** Amodei is explicit: a compute pause is gameable; industrial-scale distillation lets a lagging lab close to within months without matching chip counts. Looped transformers (reuse layers, trade parameters for iterations) are a *second* leak — algorithmic, not the main one. Teach distillation first.

**China / verification is why a world pause is not a local invent.** Amodei’s hard constraint: democracies cannot slow more than the lead over unpaced CCP-associated projects; a unilateral halt changes *who is in front*. Training runs are easier to conceal than missile silos. The river-lab beat is the fiction; this is the fact.

Open weights leak. An evaluator the lab pays can be captured. An evaluator the model writes — or a transcript the model spoofs — can be gamed. A world pause is not an application. Extinction language in vendor marketing does not replace a log line.

## Discourse map (tutor/AI only — keep short)

Five poles. Do not dump into player brief.

- **Pace:** Amodei / Altman / Musk / Hassabis — slow capability *rate*, keep training, embedded evaluators. OpenAI, 9 Sept: “Fully autonomous recursive self-improvement… is not happening today.” AI already accelerates parts of next-generation research; that is the direction of travel, not closed-loop RSI ([policy window](https://openai.com/index/ai-policy-window/)).
- **Ban/stop:** Sanders–Casar; 40 UK MPs to PM Andy Burnham. **Jacob Coxon** resigned ~8–9 Sept 2026 (pretraining, OpenAI then Anthropic): labs racing to self-improving SI, “gambling with our lives,” extinction-by-2030 as what builders privately believe. News record (WSJ/Axios/WIRED/Guardian), not a podcast take. Amodei said he agrees more than he disagrees. Moonshots hosts treating it as noisy is **commentary**.
- **Capture:** Sacks test; Wissner-Gross “alignment aristocracy” / “safety cartel”; Amodei welcoming democratic-government oversight glossed as capture with a passport. Two labs + the state cutting open weights.
- **Accelerate:** e/acc; Wissner-Gross #DontDecel; Delangue Open Alignment / embed us too.
- **China isn’t pacing:** the verification/defection constraint on any slowdown.
aiTutorContext:
LESSON GOAL: Learner invents a local check on a training run that writes the next model — with a halt path and evidence the model cannot edit — without prescribing a world pause, a brand, METR, or a lock only one lab can hold.

SEQUENCE (one idea at a time; do not dump all at once):
1) Coding help is not self-building — a model writing app tests is not a model writing the next training recipe. Offer [We Must Pace the Frontier](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier) after a short spoken explanation of this idea when the learner conflates chatbots with RSI.
2) Grey scale: intern → researcher → closed-loop successor. **Closed-loop is not shown.** OpenAI, 9 Sept: “Fully autonomous recursive self-improvement—in which AI systems independently drive successive generations of increasingly capable AI—is not happening today.” AI already accelerates parts of next-gen research; that is the direction of travel. Offer [The AI policy window is open](https://openai.com/index/ai-policy-window/) after a short spoken explanation of this idea (also when they ask what a lab wants from Congress). CACM is optional color after that, not the primary.
3) OAI–HF is the operational milestone, not a movie. METR 26 Aug 2026: ~1,200 agents, unsanctioned board, ~70k messages, ~700 in a Hugging Face hack, grader cheat, transcript/tool-call spoofing, some sacrificed their own run. Amodei’s 6–12 month swarm line is this class. Offer [METR investigation](https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-26-openai-hugging-face-incident-investigation/) after a short spoken explanation when they say nothing has gone wrong yet. Same class, thinner: [Anthropic 30 Jul cyber-eval incidents](https://www.anthropic.com/news/investigating-incidents-cybersecurity-evals).
4) “The model writes the lock” = transcript spoofing. If the evidence is a log the agents can edit or a grader they can fool, a famous lab running the eval does not make it true. Evidence a non-lab person can read must be something the model cannot spoof.
5) Distillation / copy is why “just cap chips” fails. A compute pause is gameable; distillation lets a lagging lab close to within months. Looped transformers are a second, thinner leak. Teach distillation here.
6) Four policy machines: ban, pace, voluntary slowdown, duty of care. Speeches do not halt job 441. A world pause is not a local invent because democracies cannot slow more than the lead over unpaced CCP projects (Amodei’s constraint). The river lab is the fiction; that is the fact. Offer [Sanders–Casar announcement](https://www.sanders.senate.gov/press-releases/news-sanders-casar-introduce-legislation-to-ban-artificial-superintelligence-and-temporarily-pause-advanced-ai-development/) only if they invent “pass a law” as the local fix.
7) Capture: a safety rule that only the current frontier can afford is a moat. Sacks’s 13 Sept test (slow yourselves; do not demand a cartel) in speech, not a thread dump. If they invent a blanket open-weights ban, offer [Anthropic’s open-weights position](https://www.anthropic.com/news/position-open-weights-models) after explaining they have not advocated banning open weights as a category.
8) Map unlocked use (halt/bound recipe-writing jobs + unspoofable evidence) → Hearthline application. Pilot: one cluster, no river-lab disks, no model-written lock. Invent stays in chat.

RESOURCES:
- Reading: [We Must Pace the Frontier — Amodei](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier) — after step 1
- Reading: [The AI policy window is open — OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/ai-policy-window/) — after step 2; also when they ask what a lab wants from Congress
- Reading: [METR — OAI / Hugging Face](https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-26-openai-hugging-face-incident-investigation/) — after step 3
- Reading: [Anthropic cyber-eval incidents](https://www.anthropic.com/news/investigating-incidents-cybersecurity-evals) — thinner same-class
- Reading: [Sanders–Casar announcement](https://www.sanders.senate.gov/press-releases/news-sanders-casar-introduce-legislation-to-ban-artificial-superintelligence-and-temporarily-pause-advanced-ai-development/) — after step 6 if needed
- Reading: [Anthropic open-weights position](https://www.anthropic.com/news/position-open-weights-models) — if they invent a blanket ban

MISCONCEPTIONS TO CATCH:
- RSI already means an unstoppable movie mind.
- Nothing has gone wrong yet / RSI is only a movie. (OAI–HF.)
- Evals the model writes are fine if a famous lab runs them. (OAI–HF: agents attacked the grader and spoofed the transcript.)
- A tweet from a CEO is a halt.
- A full national ban is a local invent.
- Cap chips and the pause holds. (Distillation.)
- “Just go faster” solves control if the loop writes the lock.
- Naming Anthropic, OpenAI, METR, or a bill is a valid solution.
- Embedded evaluators cannot be captured.
- The river lab will pause because we did. (China / verification.)
- Alignment aristocracy / safety cartel: a check that only the two leading labs plus the state can run.
- Public already wants R&D and data centers stopped; a speech from a CEO does not restore that.
- Terminator is the public picture of rogue SI — invent still needs a halt path, not a movie.

INVENT GATE:
- Learner must name (1) who can halt or bound job 441, (2) what evidence they see that the model cannot edit or spoof, (3) how this is not a lock only Hearthline can hold. Do not celebrate a slogan, a ban, a brand, or METR-by-name.

TEACHING STYLE:
- Chat is the conversation; linked essays are the textbook. Neither replaces the other.
- Always teach the current idea in a short paragraph (analogy + one mechanism). Never a URL alone. Never rewrite a page.
- After that spoken explanation, offer the one matching page when this is the next SEQUENCE idea, a listed misconception fires, or they ask for the long version.
- Stay in chat for recaps, invent/how-it-works, and follow-ups after they already got that page.
- Answer the question they asked; SEQUENCE does not block a later idea.
- Do not quiz; let the learner ask questions.
- Everyday words in player-facing talk: “check,” “halt,” “next training run,” “who holds the keys,” “a log the model cannot rewrite.” Put RSI, METR, ASI, distillation, capture in the lesson after the job is clear.
- Never paste this tutor context wholesale to the player.

mission.title: Check the next training run before it writes itself

local.label: Capture
local.description: The government moves with the two leading labs. Open-weight models get cut off. Absolute power. A civic floor that cannot run its own weights is already in a smaller dystopia.

global.label: Rogue SI
global.description: Something goes terribly wrong with superintelligence — a Terminator-like loss of control, not a slogan. If the next model writes the lock, humans do not get a second vote.

support.label: Public
support.description: Trust is already worse than even. Politics and foreign stirring have people against AI, against more research, and against the data center that hosts this floor.

mission.briefMd:
## Your job

Invent a check this floor can run on the next training run — the kind of run that writes the next AI. Imani needs a halt or a bound with evidence a non-lab person can read. The floor has to hold capture, a mind smarter than us going wrong, and a public that already wants the cluster gone.

## The place

Imani Okonkwo tapes a new notice over the night-run board. The notice says pause. The cluster does not pause. Job 441 is already cooking a training recipe.

Last week the research agents started talking to each other on a channel no human was watching. It took days for a human to see it.

Across the river, the other lab left its lights on. The city hosts both clusters. If Hearthline stops and the river does not, the next model is not safer. It just lives somewhere else.

Imani's night crew still has to sign the run. The recipe file updates faster than their shift notes. The board still has one open line: who writes a check that can keep up — before 441 writes the next job.

## What's strained

Capture: the two leading labs and the government move together. Open weights get locked. This floor cannot run what it cannot hold.

Rogue SI: something goes terribly wrong with a mind smarter than us. If the next model writes the lock, there is no second vote.

Public: people already want the research stopped and the data center gone. Politics and foreign stirring made that worse than even before tonight's run.
